messages.subject: acoustic playbacks in R?
parts:
Dear Seewave community

I am interested in performing animal auditory behavior experiments in R using interactive playbacks of sound files. 

For example, I would playback signal 1 (s1) from channel 1 and signal 2 (s2) from channel 2, and then part way through the trial replace s1 with s2 so that both channels are playing s2. Or many other permutations of this procedure. 

Is this possible at the moment? 

Thanks
Alex

messages.author: de80047cbc18c87e
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] acoustic playbacks in R?
parts:
Dear Alex,

I have never used R for playback experiments.

However, what you describe is probably more related to tuneR package
rather than to seewave.

See the Wave object class to manipulate left and right channels and
the function play() for playback.

You can also use several editing functions in both tuneR
(extractWave(), bind()) and seewave (cutw(), pastew(), repw() for
instance).

Sorry not to be able to help more,

Jerome
